items.stem: What is 21st June known for? What do we do on this day?
items.answer: June 21st is known as the International Day of Yoga. It was declared as such by the United Nations General Assembly in 2014 to highlight the benefits of practicing yoga and to promote global health, harmony, and peace. On this day, people around the world participate in yoga sessions, workshops, and events to celebrate the practice of yoga and its impact on physical, mental, and spiritual well-being.

items.stem: Explain the idea of unity in yoga.
items.answer: The word Yoga is derived from the Sanskrit root 'yuj', meaning 'to unite'. The practice of Yoga aims to create a union between body, mind, and spirit through three main practices: postures, breathing, and meditation.

items.stem: What does the launch of the WHO mYoga app tell us about the importance of yoga?
items.answer: mYoga. app makes people aware of how to stay active and healthy through practicing Yoga regularly. It is a valuable tool for people of all ages to make physical activity an integral part of life and reach the level needed to promote good health. It encourages them to practice Yoga. The App launched by WHO also shows that Yoga is recognized internationally.

items.stem: Describe one long-term effect that the practice of yoga can have on a person's qualities.
items.answer: Over time, those who practice yoga report lower levels of stress, and increased feelings of happiness and well-being. This is because concentrating on the postures and the breath acts as a form of meditation.

items.stem: Do you know? A few seals of the Sindhu-Sarasvati Civilisation, dating back to 2700 BC, indicate that yoga was prevalent in ancient India. Many people contributed to its development and now, yoga has spread all over the world. On 11th December 2014, the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) with 193 members accepted the proposal to celebrate '21st June' as 'International Yoga Day'.
items.answer: Yes, I am fully aware that the 21st of June is 'International Yoga Day'. Our Hon'ble Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi inaugurated the first International Day of Yoga on June 21st, 2015, on the theme Yoga for Harmony and Peace.

items.stem: Find out about two asanas and their benefits, and share your findings with your classmates and teacher. You may visit the following websites to learn more about yoga. https://www.mygov.in/campaigns/international-yoga-day/ https://www.un.org/en/observances/yoga-day https://www.mygov.in/campaigns/international-yoga-day/
items.answer: Downward Dog (Adho Mukha Svanasanu): Description: A foundational pose where the body forms an inverted V-shape. Benefits: Stretches the hamstrings, calves, and shoulders. Strengthens arms and legs. Improves blood circulation to the brain. Relieves stress and calms the mind. Tree Pose (Vrikshasana): Description: A balancing pose where one foot is placed on the inner thigh of the opposite leg, and hands are brought together above the head. Benefits: Enhances balance and stability in the legs. Strengthens thighs, calves, ankles, and spine. Improves concentration and focus. Helps in grounding and centering the mind. Who Am I? (Page 130)

items.stem: I am an odd number. Take away a letter and I become even. What number am I?
items.answer: Number 7. If you take away the letter "s," from 'seven' then it becomes 'even'.

items.stem: You go at green but stop at red. Who am I?
items.answer: You stop at a green signal when you make way for an ambulance. You run a red light when you're the one driving the ambulance.

items.stem: Three letters in my name; Backwards-forwards it's the same. I am a body part.Who am I?
items.answer: The body part that is spelled the same forward and backward is 'eye'.
